📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-ms-scheduler-api-seriesid-negative-recordid`
This is occurrence #140 (chronic pattern, first_seen 2026-06-26).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: Confirm shape via ES fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" (SeriesId=-1 signature) → compute error-rate ratio (historically marginal, ~2.5%) → root cause is a missing-guard bug in SeriesDataProvider.GetSeriesIdAsync, reproduced across 6+ distinct accounts, not account-specific → file/bump a defect for CRM Experience rather than re-diagnosing from scratch.
Open Jira: n/a (none filed)

Source alerts: n/a — degraded cycle, no Slack MCP read access this session. Source: DD monitor 303750093, synthetic fire time 2026-07-10T22:30:34Z (self-recovered by scan time).

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/303750093 (state: OK at scan time)
  • ES aggregate: fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" AND level.keyword:"Error", 2026-07-10T22:00:34Z–22:30:34Z → 10 hits, dominant message "Get Series Info failed for recordId -1" (same SeriesId=-1 bug class as this KB's documented signature, under a slightly different message wording than the KB's exact-string evidence_query — the narrower query alone returned 0 hits; broadening to level:Error surfaced the real recurrence).
  • This-window concentration: 10/10 hits on ms-scheduler-api (single-service, consistent with prior occurrences)

Note: this recurrence resurfaces via the every-10th-occurrence rule (occurrence #140, last posted 2026-07-10T12:08:35Z, ~23h ago — still within the 24h suppression window) — routine resurfacing of a known chronic pattern. Follow-up: this KB's evidence_query text should be broadened to also match "Get Series Info failed for recordId -1".

🚨 *new alert — needs human* (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: code  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)

Symptoms:
  - DD monitor 299251404 ("Service tables-fields has a high error rate on env:prod") fired at 2026-07-11T00:13:24Z, self-recovered by scan time
  - ES message.keyword aggregate for tables-fields/level:Error in the fire window: 2 hits, sole bucket "SaveFieldLegacyExtended Failed"
  - Full sample: System.NullReferenceException at Models.Converters.HelperConverter.GetFields (HelperConverter.cs:123 per local clone HEAD 2026-04-24 — 78 days stale, methodcrm-org GH_TOKEN 403 blocks a fresh fetch, NOT independently confirmed against current prod), called from GetView, called from API.Controllers.FieldController.SaveFieldLegacyExtended. Line 123 dereferences `fieldModel.Column.Type` without a null check.

Trace IDs: dd_trace_id 6a51890f000000005c6db434026a6e5c (and a second near-identical trace ~0.4s later)
Likely cause: NullReferenceException when `fieldModel.Column` is null inside HelperConverter.GetFields, reached via the field-delete/edit path (SaveFieldLegacyExtended → EditView → GetView → GetFields).
Suggested next action: file defect for Admin team; new KB entry `ki-2026-07-11-tables-fields-savefieldlegacyextended-nre` written this cycle (fix_status: needs-human) — this is a THIRD distinct bug signature sharing monitor 299251404 alongside ki-2026-07-02 (FieldTableNameRef Is Null) and ki-2026-07-06 (AlterTableToDropColumn DDL syntax error); recommend splitting this DD monitor into per-error-type checks.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #41 since 2026-07-04.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: Pull sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:<name>,env:prod}.as_rate() over a multi-hour window — expect a genuine but brief dip below the monitor's floor, not a data gap. Confirm service:<name> status:error returns 0 in DD Logs. Check the sibling outbound-5xx/P95-latency monitor for the same service — if also OK, this is the benign quiet-period pattern. Escalate only if unresolved after ~1h or a sibling error/latency monitor co-fires.
Open Jira: n/a (none filed)

This is occurrence #7 in the last 7 days.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Growth` (`@growth` / `#team-growth`)
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: DD metric p90:trace.aspnet.request{env:prod,service:signup,resource_name:post_/*} in the alert window -- expect only 1-3 non-zero points (low traffic) with one point near/above 12s. 2) Confirm no errors: service:signup status:error DD Logs should be 0. 3) Do not treat as an incident on a single occurrence -- self-recovers within one eval window every time so far. 4) Recommend to Growth: raise the threshold or gate on minimum sample count so a single slow request can't dominate p90 on a low-traffic endpoint.
